items.plain: A hermit gives up a broken-up, piecemeal world so that he can enjoy the whole world fully and without interruption.
items.core_idea: The hermit leaves fragments to enjoy the whole

items.plain: Between the scholar and the poet lies open ground. A scholar who crosses it becomes wise; a poet who crosses it becomes a prophet.
items.core_idea: Scholar and poet each grow by crossing toward the other

items.plain: I saw philosophers in the market carrying their heads in baskets and shouting that wisdom was for sale. Poor things: they have to sell their minds to feed their hearts.
items.core_idea: Philosophers sell their minds to feed their hearts

items.plain: A philosopher pitied a street sweeper for his hard, dirty work. When the philosopher said his own job was studying human minds, deeds and desires, the sweeper smiled and pitied him too.
items.core_idea: Studying human nature can be the dirtier job

items.plain: The person who listens to the truth is no less than the person who speaks it.
items.core_idea: Hearing truth matters as much as speaking it

items.plain: No person can mark the line between what we need and what is luxury. Only angels can, and angels are both wise and a little sad.
items.core_idea: Only angels can separate needs from luxuries

items.plain: Generosity means giving more than you can afford, and pride means taking less than you need.
items.core_idea: Generosity gives beyond means; pride takes below need

items.plain: Really you owe nothing to any one person. You owe everything to everyone.
items.core_idea: We owe everything to everyone, not to anyone

items.plain: Everyone who lived before us still lives with us now. None of us would want to be a rude host to them.
items.core_idea: The dead live among us as our guests

items.plain: Whoever longs the most lives the longest.
items.core_idea: Longing lengthens life

items.plain: People say a bird in the hand is worth more than many in the bush. But a bird and a feather still out of reach are worth more; chasing that feather is life itself.
items.core_idea: Chasing what is out of reach is life itself

items.plain: Great beauty holds me captive, but an even greater beauty sets me free, even from itself.
items.core_idea: The greatest beauty frees rather than captures

items.plain: Beauty glows more brightly in the heart of someone who longs for it than in the eyes of someone who sees it.
items.core_idea: Longing for beauty outshines seeing it

items.plain: I admire people who show me their minds and honour those who show me their dreams. So why do I feel shy, even a little ashamed, before someone who serves me?
items.core_idea: Being served brings an odd shame

items.plain: Talented people once took pride in serving princes. Now they take pride in serving the poor.
items.core_idea: The gifted now find honour serving the poor

items.plain: The angels know that too many practical people live off the hard work of dreamers.
items.core_idea: Practical people often live off dreamers' labour

items.plain: Wit is often a mask. Pull it off and you will find either an annoyed genius or mere cleverness showing off.
items.core_idea: Wit often masks irritation or showing off

items.plain: Only people who carry secrets in their own hearts can guess the secrets in ours.
items.core_idea: It takes secrets to sense secrets

items.plain: Anyone who will share your joy but not your pain loses the key to one of the seven gates of Paradise.
items.core_idea: Friends must share pain as well as joy

items.plain: Yes, Nirvana exists: it is in leading your sheep to green grass, putting your child to sleep, and writing the last line of your poem.
items.core_idea: Nirvana is found in ordinary fulfilled tasks

items.plain: We choose our joys and our sorrows long before we live through them.
items.core_idea: We choose our joys and sorrows in advance

items.plain: Sadness is only a wall standing between two gardens.
items.core_idea: Sadness separates two good places

items.plain: When your joy or your sorrow grows great, the world around you shrinks.
items.core_idea: Great joy or sorrow shrinks the world

items.plain: Desire is half of being alive; not caring is half of being dead.
items.core_idea: Desire is life; indifference is death

items.plain: The bitterest part of today's sorrow is remembering yesterday's joy.
items.core_idea: Past joy makes present sorrow bitterest

items.plain: People tell me I must choose between this world's pleasures and the next world's peace. I have chosen both, because I know the Supreme Poet wrote only one poem, and it fits together perfectly.
items.core_idea: This world and the next are one poem

items.plain: Faith is an oasis in the heart that the caravan of thinking will never reach.
items.core_idea: Thinking cannot reach faith

items.plain: When you reach your highest point, you will desire only for the sake of desiring, hunger for hunger itself, and thirst for a greater thirst.
items.core_idea: At our height, longing becomes its own aim

items.plain: If you tell your secrets to the wind, do not blame the wind for passing them on to the trees.
items.core_idea: Do not blame others for secrets you spread

items.plain: Turtles can tell you more about the roads than hares can.
items.core_idea: The slow traveller knows the road best

items.plain: It is strange that creatures without backbones have the hardest shells.
items.core_idea: The spineless often wear the hardest shells

items.plain: Be thankful you do not have to live down a famous father or a rich uncle. Above all, be thankful no one will have to live down your fame or your wealth.
items.core_idea: Be glad no fame or wealth burdens anyone

items.plain: A person who envies me is praising me without knowing it.
items.core_idea: Envy is unknowing praise

items.plain: For a long time you were a dream in your mother's sleep, and then she woke up to give birth to you.
items.core_idea: Each child begins as a mother's dream

items.plain: Some of our children justify our lives, and some are only our regrets.
items.core_idea: Children can be justifications or regrets

items.plain: When night comes and you feel dark too, lie down and be dark on purpose. If you are still dark in the morning, get up and tell the day so. Pretending to night and day is foolish; they would laugh.
items.core_idea: Own your darkness openly instead of pretending

items.plain: A mountain hidden in mist is still not a hill, and an oak in the rain is still not a weeping willow.
items.core_idea: Passing conditions do not change true nature

items.plain: When I stood before you like a clear mirror, you saw your own image in me and said you loved me. But really you loved yourself, seen in me.
items.core_idea: Some love is self-love seen in another

items.plain: When you enjoy loving your neighbour, it stops being a virtue.
items.core_idea: Love that is enjoyed is no longer virtue

items.plain: Love that is not always welling up fresh is always dying.
items.core_idea: Love must keep renewing or it dies

items.plain: You cannot be young and understand youth at the same time. Youth is too busy living to know, and knowledge is too busy searching for itself to live.
items.core_idea: Youth lives without knowing; knowledge knows without living

items.plain: Watching from a window, you might call a nun noble and a prostitute shameful. But listen quietly and a voice says one seeks it in prayer, the other in pain, and both have room for its spirit.
items.core_idea: The saint and the sinner both seek the divine

items.plain: A great person has two hearts: one that bleeds and one that holds back and endures.
items.core_idea: Greatness both feels pain and patiently endures

items.plain: If someone tells a lie that hurts no one, why not think of it kindly: their facts were too small a house for their imagination, so they moved somewhere roomier?
items.core_idea: Harmless lies are imagination outgrowing facts

items.plain: Behind every closed door lies a deeply sealed mystery.
items.core_idea: Every closed door hides a mystery

items.plain: Waiting is the sound of time's hoofbeats.
items.core_idea: In waiting we feel time passing

items.plain: What if trouble were a new window opened in the eastern wall of your house, where the sun rises?
items.core_idea: Trouble may open a new window of light

items.plain: You may forget someone you laughed with, but you will never forget someone you cried with.
items.core_idea: Shared tears bind us more than shared laughter

items.plain: Salt must be strangely holy, since it is found both in our tears and in the sea.
items.core_idea: Salt links our tears to the sea

items.plain: You are only a small piece of your huge true self: a mouth looking for bread, and a hand that blindly holds a cup for a thirsty mouth.
items.core_idea: We are fragments of a far greater self

items.plain: If you could rise even a little above race, nation and self, you would truly become like God.
items.core_idea: Rising above race, nation and self is godlike

items.plain: I would not complain about the sea at low tide. The ship is sound and our Captain capable; it is only your stomach that is upset.
items.core_idea: Our unease is not the voyage's fault

items.plain: What we long for and cannot reach is dearer to us than what we already have.
items.core_idea: The unattained is dearer than the attained

items.plain: From a cloud you would see no borders between countries and no markers between farms. It is a pity you cannot sit on a cloud.
items.core_idea: From above, our borders disappear

items.plain: Long ago seven white doves flew up a mountain, and one watcher noticed a black spot on one wing. Now the valley's people tell of seven black doves.
items.core_idea: A small flaw grows into the whole story

items.plain: In autumn I buried my sorrows in my garden. In spring they grew into flowers unlike any others, and my neighbours asked me for their seeds for their own gardens.
items.core_idea: Buried sorrows can bloom into beauty others want

items.plain: It is misery to hold out an empty hand and receive nothing. But it is hopelessness to hold out a full hand and find no one to take what you offer.
items.core_idea: Worse than receiving nothing is having none receive

items.plain: I long for eternity because there I will meet the poems I never wrote and the pictures I never painted.
items.core_idea: Eternity holds our unmade works

items.plain: Art is a step from nature toward the Infinite.
items.core_idea: Art moves from nature toward the Infinite

items.plain: Even hands that make crowns of thorns are better than hands that do nothing.
items.core_idea: Any work beats idleness

items.plain: Our holiest tears never look for our eyes.
items.core_idea: The deepest grief is not wept outwardly

items.plain: Every person descends from every king and every slave who ever lived.
items.core_idea: All of us share every ancestor

items.plain: Did Judas's mother love her son any less than Mary loved Jesus?
items.core_idea: A mother's love does not depend on the child

items.plain: Three miracles of Jesus are missing from the Bible: he was a man like us, he had a sense of humour, and he knew he was a conqueror even while defeated.
items.core_idea: Jesus's humanity and humour were miracles too

items.plain: Crucified One, you are crucified on my heart, and the nails through your hands pierce my heart too. A stranger passing this place tomorrow will not know two bled here; he will think it one man's blood.
items.core_idea: The believer bleeds with the crucified Christ

items.plain: The Blessed Mountain is the highest in the world. Whoever reaches its top wants only to come down and be with those in the deepest valley; that is why it is called blessed.
items.core_idea: True height makes us want to serve the lowest

items.plain: Every thought I have locked up in words, I must set free through my actions.
items.core_idea: Words must be freed through deeds

items.plain: Krishna tells the prince that the senses' heat and cold, sorrow and joy, are brief and changing; bear them as the wise do. The soul that stays calm through sorrow and joy alike lives the undying life.
items.core_idea: A calm soul through joy and sorrow is undying

items.plain: The spirit was never born and will never end; beginnings and endings are dreams. It stays birthless, deathless and unchanging forever, untouched by death even when its body seems dead.
items.core_idea: The spirit is never born and never dies

items.plain: Just as a person takes off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the spirit lightly sets aside its body and moves on to a new home.
items.core_idea: The spirit changes bodies like clothes

items.plain: Krishna tells the prince that living things come from the unseen and return to the unseen at death; only the in-between is seen. So what is there to grieve?
items.core_idea: Birth and death are unseen; why grieve?

items.plain: Krishna says: do not crave. Do right for its own sake, not for its results. Keep working, make your work your devotion, set self aside, and stay even in good or bad; that evenness is Yoga.
items.core_idea: Act rightly without attachment to results

items.plain: Krishna says a right action is worth far less than a rightly thinking mind. Take refuge in your soul and make your heaven there, and scorn those who are good only for the rewards.
items.core_idea: A right mind matters more than right acts

items.plain: Someone who is not crushed by sorrow or carried away by joy, who lives beyond passion, fear and anger, and rests in calm, deep contemplation, is the true sage.
items.core_idea: The sage stays steady in sorrow and joy

items.plain: Dwelling on sense objects breeds attraction, then desire, passion and recklessness, until memory, purpose and mind are lost. But handling them without love or hate, with a free soul in charge, brings tranquillity, an end to earthly pain, and peace.
items.core_idea: Dwelling on desires ruins; mastering them brings peace

items.plain: Like the ocean, which takes in rivers from every land yet never overflows, the perfected person takes in the world's tempting streams without being stirred and remains the same sea.
items.core_idea: The perfected person absorbs desire unmoved, like the sea

items.plain: It is better to do your own task as best you can, even failing, than to take up another's, however good it looks. Dying in your own duty is no harm; seekers of other paths keep wandering.
items.core_idea: Better your own duty, imperfectly, than another's

items.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that even if he were the worst of all wrongdoers, the ship of Truth would carry him safely across the sea of his wrongs.
items.core_idea: Truth carries even the worst sinner across

items.plain: Do not be too happy when joy comes or too sad when grief comes; stay steady and fixed on Brahma.
items.core_idea: Stay steady in Brahma through joy and grief

items.plain: Sense pleasures are wombs that breed certain grief; they begin and end, and the wise take no delight in them. But whoever learns, while still in the body, to master lust and anger is blessed.
items.core_idea: Mastering lust and anger brings blessing

items.plain: Krishna says true religion is not for those who fast or feast too much, oversleep, or exhaust themselves with vigils. True piety is moderation in eating, rest, play, wishes and deeds, with timely sleep and waking.
items.core_idea: True piety is moderation in all things

items.plain: The Yogi's mind is like a lamp burning steadily out of the wind: shut away from the storms of the senses and burning brightly toward Heaven.
items.core_idea: A yogi's mind is a sheltered, steady flame

items.plain: Each time the heart breaks loose, wild and wavering, rein it back under the soul's control. Perfect bliss grows only in a calm heart, a spirit free of passion and wrong, given to the Infinite.
items.core_idea: Keep bringing the wandering heart back

items.plain: Krishna admits to Arjuna that the human heart is truly hard to restrain and always wavering. Yet it can be tamed through habit, by practising self-command.
items.core_idea: The restless heart is tamed by practice

items.plain: Krishna says he is the freshness of water, the light of moon and sun, the sacred word, the scent of wet earth, the breath in all that moves, the root of everything, and the wisdom of the wise.
items.core_idea: God is the essence within all things

items.plain: Krishna says that whoever offers him, with faith and love, even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or some water, he accepts that offering made with a loving heart.
items.core_idea: God accepts the humblest gift given in love

items.plain: Krishna says that if someone living an evil life turns their mind straight to him, count them among the good: they have chosen the high road, will soon be righteous, and will reach unchanging peace.
items.core_idea: Turning to God makes even the wicked good

items.plain: Krishna says that intellect, skill, endurance, self-control, truthfulness, calm, joy and grief, birth and death, fear and courage, shame and honour, gentleness, peace, laughter, tears, devotion, generosity and the will to help all come as his gifts.
items.core_idea: Every human quality is God's gift

items.plain: Krishna says the wise, knowing him as the source of all, fix their hearts on him and find happiness and peace. To those who love him he gives a clear mind, and dwells within to dispel their ignorance.
items.core_idea: God lights the minds of those who love him

items.plain: Krishna says he is the Spirit seated deep in every creature's heart: they come from him, live by him, and leave at his word.
items.core_idea: God is the Spirit in every heart

items.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna he can be known, seen and entered only through full service, perfect faith and total surrender. Whoever does everything for him, finds him in all things, worships always and loves all he has made comes to him.
items.core_idea: God is reached through total love and surrender

items.plain: Krishna says: if you cannot keep your mind on him, do not despair. Worship him; failing that, work for him; failing that, bring him your failure and let go of results. Eternal peace lies very near renunciation.
items.core_idea: Whatever your weakness, God offers a lower step

items.plain: Krishna says he loves the person who neither troubles others nor is troubled by them, is free of anger, beyond gladness, grief and fear, calm, pure and balanced, working with him yet detached from all work.
items.core_idea: God loves the calm, detached, untroubled person

items.plain: Krishna loves the person who treats friend and foe alike, meets shame and glory, pleasure and pain with equal peace, is free of desire, unmoved by praise or slander, and steadfast in him.
items.core_idea: God loves the one who stays even in all things

items.plain: Krishna lists the signs of someone on the path to heavenly birth: fearlessness, striving for wisdom, generosity, self-restraint, humility, truthfulness, harmlessness, slowness to anger, letting go easily, kindness to sufferers, contentment, patience, purity and no thirst for revenge or self-importance.
items.core_idea: The virtues that mark the path to heaven

items.plain: Krishna says the doors to Hell, through which people go to ruin, are three: lust, anger and greed. Avoid all three.
items.core_idea: Lust, anger and greed are hell's doors

items.plain: Words that hurt no one, that are always true, gentle and kind, and the words spoken in reading sacred scripture: these make up true religion in speech.
items.core_idea: Kind, true speech is a form of worship

items.plain: Krishna says true action is doing your duty faithfully because it is right, not clinging to the work or its reward, untroubled by failure or success. No one embodied can stop acting; giving up the profit is true renunciation.
items.core_idea: True renunciation is acting without wanting rewards

fix.display_text:
But, Arjun!
Abstaining from attachment to the work,
Abstaining from rewardment in the work,
While yet one doeth it full faithfully,
Saying, "'Tis right to do!" that is "true" act
And abstinence! Who doeth duties so,
Unvexed if his work fail, if it succeed
Unflattered, in his own heart justified,
Quit of debates and doubts, his is "true" act:
For, being in the body, none may stand
Wholly aloof from act; yet, who abstains
From profit of his acts is abstinent.
fix.reason: stray space inside quote; missing apostrophe in 'Tis

items.plain: Krishna says the rightful doer acts without self-seeking, humble, determined and steady, the same in good or bad fortune, content simply to do right; that person truly acts.
items.core_idea: The true doer acts humbly, without self-seeking

fix.display_text:
There is the "rightful" doer. He who acts
Free from self-seeking, humble, resolute,
Steadfast, in good or evil hap the same,
Content to do aright--he "truly" acts.
fix.reason: missing space after quote; hyphen should be dash

items.plain: Good pleasure lasts and banishes pain for ever. It tastes bitter as poison at first but later sweet as the nectar of immortality. Drink it; it rises from the spirit's deep contentment.
items.core_idea: True pleasure is bitter first, sweet later

items.plain: Krishna says your own work done with faults beats another's done well. Do not drop your natural duty because it carries blame; every work has some, as every flame has smoke. Perfection comes through renouncing results.
items.core_idea: Do your own duty though it is imperfect

items.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is precious and well loved. Give him your heart, worship him, serve him and cling to him in faith and love, and you will come to him; he promises, because Arjuna is dear to him.
items.core_idea: God promises to receive those who love him

items.plain: It is empty to follow bodily desires that end in misery, to want a long life but not a good one, to think only of this life, and to love what quickly passes instead of hurrying toward eternal joy.
items.core_idea: Living only for passing things is vanity

items.plain: However much you know, there is far more you do not. Do not be proud; admit your ignorance, since many know Scripture better than you. To learn anything worthwhile, love being unknown and counted as nothing.
items.core_idea: Admit your ignorance and love being unknown

items.plain: The best lesson is to judge yourself humbly and others kindly. Even if your neighbour sins openly, do not think yourself better; you cannot know how long you will stay good. We are all weak; count no one weaker.
items.core_idea: Think humbly of yourself and kindly of others

items.plain: Nothing troubles you more than your own undisciplined heart. A good person plans inwardly and submits all to right reason. The hardest battle is self-mastery, and that should be our aim: growing daily stronger than self.
items.core_idea: The hardest battle is mastering yourself

items.plain: In this life every perfection has some flaw. Humbly knowing yourself leads to God more surely than deep learning. Learning is not wrong, but a good conscience and a holy life are better than everything.
items.core_idea: Humble self-knowledge leads to God better than learning

items.plain: Only someone with great love is truly great. The truly great think themselves small; the truly wise count earthly things as rubbish to gain Christ; the truly learned do God's will instead of their own.
items.core_idea: True greatness is love, humility and doing God's will

items.plain: Wisdom means not rushing to act, not clinging to your opinions, not believing or repeating all you hear, and taking advice from wise, good people. The humbler you are and the more obedient to God, the wiser and calmer.
items.core_idea: Wisdom is humility, caution and good counsel

items.plain: Wanting anything too much makes you restless. The proud and greedy never rest; the humble live in peace. Someone not yet dead to self is easily tempted by small things, and sad and irritable when giving up pleasures.
items.core_idea: Excessive desire breeds restlessness; humility brings peace

items.plain: Life is empty if you trust people or created things. Do not be ashamed to serve others for love of Jesus Christ. Hope in God, do what you can, and God will help; he resists the proud, favours the humble.
items.core_idea: Trust God, not yourself or other people
